author: arcprize
summary: ARC Prize’s October 13 announcement reports DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at about 3% with its provider adapter and below 1% with the standard harness. The original linked verified-results table, refreshed October 14, gives a matched Low-reasoning comparison of 3.26% versus 0.35%; its headline best configurations differ in reasoning level. Organizer model evaluation, separate from Kaggle team submissions.
whyItMatters: Public original read without sign-in in the in-app browser; linked primary results table independently read. Organizer evaluation, separate from Kaggle team standings.

author: arcprize
summary: ARC Prize announces Tufa Labs reclaimed first on the ARC-AGI-3 public Kaggle board with roughly 69%, up from roughly 56%. This is the author’s dated October 13 observation; refresh standings before publication.
whyItMatters: Organizer confirmation of a consequential team result already covered in the newspaper’s morning/afternoon reporting; no methods disclosed.

author: OCEANVIN10
summary: OCEAN highlighted the Memento 3 preprint. Its authors report that a fixed language model revises an external rulebook and executable world model; on the 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, they report clearing every level with fewer actions than the human baseline. These are author-reported results on the public set.
whyItMatters: A new ARC-AGI-3 research lead for the edition desk. The paper provides a concrete mechanism and results, but the public tutorial set cannot establish private-game performance.

author: arcprize
summary: ARC Prize announced a new 2026 ARC-AGI-2 Kaggle high of 88.06% by Tufa Labs and said a $150,000 bonus would be split among teams scoring above 85%.
whyItMatters: A public-board threshold announcement and major standings lead; the post does not establish a final private score.

author: arcprize
summary: ARC Prize announced Yi-Chia Chen at 59.17% on the 2026 ARC-AGI-3 Kaggle board, taking the lead over Tufa Labs.
whyItMatters: Historical October 9 standings announcement, newly inventoried as a Chollet repost; not a fresh score move. Original and visible context re-read; existing independently verified public visibility preserved.

author: fchollet
summary: Chollet argues that autonomous robotics needs causality and discrete reasoning beyond autoregressive sampling, and praises Biwei Huang’s Aether AI work. His quote refers to Huang’s October 12 CRIS-0 announcement; it is not an October 14 model release or a Kaggle result.
whyItMatters: New public founder research lead. Original and visible conversation read; public body independently readable without sign-in. Linked CRIS-0 technical project page read: explicit task state, verification, retry/replan; reported robotics work, no disclosed ARC recipe.

author: iiiiitsu_ne
summary: Japanese translation: Even with a 2.5-point improvement, I have actually dropped from rank 31. The attached native Kaggle share says Moved up to rank 35 for ARC-AGI-2. This is the author’s posting-time comparison, distinct from the saved rolling board event and later rank.
whyItMatters: Own standings voice. Kaggle nisshokuitsuki directly links @iiiiitsu_ne; current ARC-2 Odd Dice roster contains that handle. Original body/date independently readable without sign-in.

author: fchollet
summary: Chollet argues that the ideal scientific outcome of AI is to enable millions of human scientists to pursue their curiosity more ambitiously, rather than concentrating expensive proprietary systems in a few labs tackling prestige problems.
whyItMatters: A fresh public founder statement at 11:43 pm Eastern on October 13. This is his view of AI-aided science, not a new release or ARC contest result. Original post read in signed-in Chrome with ordinary public engagement controls and no subscriber label; the separately read Subs feed retains its explicit private labels.

author: mikeknoop
summary: Knoop takes stock of what he sees as rapid AI disruption in coding, mathematics, games and app building, and argues that the changes create opportunities for builders.
whyItMatters: A founder perspective on AI progress. His broad disruption and cryptography claims remain attributed commentary, separate from contest standings.
